```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site.R"))

n_interviews <- nrow(respondents)
n_persons <- sum(respondents$person_first)
years <- range(str_sub(respondents$interview_month, 1, 4))

# one row per survey
surveys <- respondents |>
  summarise(
    provider = first(provider),
    wave = first(wave),
    age_min = min(age),
    age_max = max(age),
    n = n(),
    first_month = ym(min(interview_month)),
    last_month = ym(max(interview_month)),
    recontacts = sum(sample_type == "Recontact"),
    .by = dataset
  ) |>
  arrange(dataset) |>
  mutate(
    fieldwork = if_else(
      year(first_month) == year(last_month),
      str_c(format(first_month, "%B"), " to ", format(last_month, "%B %Y")),
      str_c(format(first_month, "%B %Y"), " to ", format(last_month, "%B %Y"))
    ),
    answers = if_else(provider == "Survation", "A parent, then the child", "The young person")
  )

# ages covered by each provider and their overlap
provider_ages <- respondents |>
  summarise(min = min(age), max = max(age), .by = provider) |>
  mutate(provider = word(provider, 1)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(min, max)) |>
  mutate(name = str_c(provider, "_", name)) |>
  select(name, value) |>
  deframe()
overlap <- c(
  max(provider_ages[["Gallup_min"]], provider_ages[["Survation_min"]]),
  min(provider_ages[["Gallup_max"]], provider_ages[["Survation_max"]])
)

n_survation_18 <- sum(respondents$dataset == "Survation W2" & respondents$age == 18)

# share of Gallup W2 interviews in November and December 2025
gallup_w2_late <- respondents |>
  filter(dataset == "Gallup W2") |>
  summarise(share = mean(interview_month %in% c("2025-11", "2025-12"))) |>
  pull(share) |>
  percent(accuracy = 1)

# mean of the six 0 to 10 items asked in all four surveys, per respondent
scale_scores <- respondents |>
  mutate(score = rowMeans(pick(ftp1_UK, ftp2_UK, ftp3_UK, ftp4_UK, ftp5_UK, lr), na.rm = TRUE))

score_dataset <- scale_scores |>
  summarise(mean = mean(score), .by = dataset) |>
  mutate(dataset = as.character(dataset)) |>
  deframe()
score_others <- score_dataset[names(score_dataset) != "Survation W1"]

score_survation_w1 <- scale_scores |>
  filter(dataset == "Survation W1") |>
  mutate(group = if_else(panel, "panel", "others")) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(score), .by = group) |>
  deframe()

# panel links by provider
links <- panel |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    strict = sum(link_age_diff %in% 1:2 & link_same_gender),
    .by = provider
  ) |>
  mutate(provider = word(provider, 1))
link_n <- deframe(select(links, provider, n))
link_strict <- deframe(select(links, provider, strict))

# topics covered by the questions on this site
survey_cols <- c(
  "Gallup W1" = "n_gallup_w1",
  "Survation W1" = "n_survation_w1",
  "Gallup W2" = "n_gallup_w2",
  "Survation W2" = "n_survation_w2"
)

questions <- variables |>
  filter(!block %in% c("Identifiers and linking", "Interview")) |>
  mutate(topic = coalesce(topic, block))

n_questions <- nrow(questions)
n_all_four <- questions |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(unname(survey_cols)), \(x) x > 0)) |>
  nrow()
asked_by_survey <- colSums(select(questions, all_of(unname(survey_cols))) > 0) |>
  set_names(names(survey_cols))
```

The IP-PAD UK data combine four online surveys of young people in the United Kingdom, carried out between `r years[1]` and `r years[2]` by two fieldwork providers that each ran two waves. The combined file has one row per interview and holds `r comma(n_interviews)` interviews with `r comma(n_persons)` young people. Apart from two questions about the future that only Survation asked, it includes only questions asked in at least two of the surveys.

## The four surveys

::: {.data-table}
```{r}
#| label: table-surveys
surveys |>
  transmute(
    Survey = str_c(dataset, "<span class='survey-sub'>", provider, ", wave ", wave, "</span>"),
    Ages = str_c("<span class='nowrap'>", age_min, "–", age_max, "</span>"),
    Interviews = comma(n),
    Fieldwork = fieldwork,
    `Recontacted from wave 1` = if_else(recontacts == 0, "<span class='none'>None</span>", comma(recontacts)),
    `Who answered` = answers
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "l", "r", "l", "r", "l"),
    escape = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table"'
  )
```
:::

Gallup respondents answered all questions themselves. In the Survation surveys, a parent first gave consent and reported the child's age, gender, region and type of place, before the child answered the rest of the questionnaire. In both second waves, the providers invited their first-wave respondents back and then added new respondents. Because few Gallup respondents returned, Gallup W2 added a separate sample of 22 to 26 year olds, and Survation W2 also admitted `r n_survation_18` respondents aged 18 outside its quota.

## When the surveys were in the field

::: {.how-to-read}
Each row shows one survey. The bars give the number of interviews in each month, on the same scale for all four surveys.
:::

```{r}
#| label: plot-timeline
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| fig-alt: !expr str_c("Monthly number of interviews in each of the four surveys, from May 2024 to November 2026. Gallup W1 ran in May and June 2024. Gallup W2 ran from May 2025 to January 2026, with ", gallup_w2_late, " of its interviews in November and December 2025. Survation W1 ran from July to September 2025, during the Gallup W2 fieldwork. Survation W2 ran from August to November 2026, mostly in October.")
timeline <- respondents |>
  count(dataset, interview_month) |>
  mutate(month = ym(interview_month) + days(14))

ggplot(timeline, aes(x = month, y = n, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_col(width = 26) +
  facet_wrap(~dataset, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(ym("2024-05"), ym("2026-11"), by = "6 months"),
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    limits = c(ym("2024-04"), ym("2026-12"))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1000), labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = "Survation W1 was in the field while Gallup W2 was running",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = site_caption
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = brand[["rule"]], linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.3, "lines")
  )
```

Three of the surveys carried out most of their interviews within two or three months. Gallup W2 began in May 2025 with a few interviews each month, and `r gallup_w2_late` of its interviews took place in November and December 2025, when the 22 to 26 year olds were added.

## Before comparing surveys

The four surveys share most of their questions but were not designed as one sample. The differences below matter whenever answers are compared across surveys, and the [explorer](explore.qmd) lets you check whether a pattern holds in each survey separately.

- **Different age ranges.** The two providers overlap only at ages `r overlap[1]` to `r overlap[2]`, so a difference between Gallup and Survation can reflect age as much as the provider.
- **Wave is not time.** The variable `wave` counts the waves within each provider. Survation W1 was in the field in the summer of 2025, while Gallup W2 was still running, so the fieldwork dates are the better guide to timing.
- **Not weighted.** All respondents come from online panels and the data are not weighted, so the results describe the young people who took part rather than all young people in the UK.
- **Different quality checks.** Each survey removed careless or automated answers by its own rules. Gallup W1, for example, kept respondents who failed its attention check, whereas Survation removed those who failed two checks.
- **Survation W1 scores higher on 0 to 10 scales.** Averaged over the five party ratings and the left-right scale, Survation W1 respondents score `r number(score_dataset[["Survation W1"]], 0.1)`, against `r number(min(score_others), 0.1)` to `r number(max(score_others), 0.1)` in the other surveys. Those who took part again a year later had already answered much like the other surveys in the first wave (`r number(score_survation_w1[["panel"]], 0.1)`), which suggests that the difference lies in who took part. The insight on [left and right](insights/uk/left-right/index.qmd) shows an example.
- **Few and uncertain panel links.** Only `r link_n[["Gallup"]]` Gallup and `r link_n[["Survation"]]` Survation respondents took part in both waves of their provider. Judged by age and gender, `r link_strict[["Gallup"]]` of the Gallup links and `r link_strict[["Survation"]]` of the Survation links are plausible. Survation links run through the parent's panel account, so a sibling may have answered in some cases.
- **Small wording differences.** A few questions were worded slightly differently between the surveys, such as the introduction to the party ratings. The codebook notes each of these differences.

## What the data cover

This website uses `r n_questions` questions from the combined file, grouped by topic below. Of these, `r n_all_four` were asked in all four surveys, while Survation W2 asked fewer of the shared questions (`r asked_by_survey[["Survation W2"]]`).

::: {.data-table}
```{r}
#| label: table-topics
topic_order <- c(
  "Interest and participation", "Ideology", "Party feelings", "Issue attitudes",
  "Ideological labels", "Democracy and populism", "Trust in institutions",
  "Living and belonging", "Outlook and personality", "Demographics"
)
stopifnot(setequal(topic_order, questions$topic))

questions |>
  summarise(
    Questions = n(),
    across(all_of(unname(survey_cols)), \(x) sum(x > 0)),
    .by = topic
  ) |>
  arrange(match(topic, topic_order)) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(unname(survey_cols)),
      \(x) case_when(
        x == Questions ~ "All",
        x == 0 ~ "<span class='none'>None</span>",
        .default = as.character(x)
      )
    )
  ) |>
  rename(Topic = topic, all_of(survey_cols)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    escape = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table"'
  )
```
:::

## Search the questions

Search by variable name, question wording or topic to see which surveys asked a question.

::: {.variable-search}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
variables = FileAttachment("data/variables.csv").csv({typed: true})

type_labels = ({
  number: "Number",
  ordered: "Ordered categories",
  factor: "Categories",
  logical: "Yes or no",
  text: "Text"
})

survey_counts = [
  ["Gallup W1", "n_gallup_w1"],
  ["Survation W1", "n_survation_w1"],
  ["Gallup W2", "n_gallup_w2"],
  ["Survation W2", "n_survation_w2"]
]

variable_rows = variables.map(d => {
  const asked = survey_counts.filter(([, col]) => d[col] > 0).map(([survey]) => survey)
  return {
    name: d.name,
    label: d.short_label,
    topic: d.topic ?? d.block,
    type: type_labels[d.type] ?? d.type,
    surveys: asked.length === 4 ? "All four" : asked.join(", ")
  }
})

viewof variable_query = Inputs.search(variable_rows, {
  placeholder: "For example trust, climate or lr",
  label: "Search the list"
})

narrow = width < 620

Inputs.table(variable_query, {
  columns: narrow
    ? ["name", "label", "surveys"]
    : ["name", "label", "topic", "type", "surveys"],
  header: {
    name: "Name",
    label: "Question",
    topic: "Topic",
    type: "Type",
    surveys: "Asked in"
  },
  width: narrow
    ? {name: "28%", label: "44%", surveys: "28%"}
    : {name: "15%", label: "35%", topic: "18%", type: "13%", surveys: "19%"},
  layout: "fixed",
  rows: 24
})
```
:::

## Getting the data

The combined data and their documentation will be released in the near future, and we will post a link to them on this website. The data will come as csv and RData files, with copies for SPSS and Stata, together with a codebook that notes how each question was asked in each survey.

They will be released under a [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) licence, so you may share and adapt them as long as you cite them as given on the [About page](about.qmd#citation).
